why: The build receipt records the paths of the machine that produced the artifacts (a Windows temp directory). check-g2-artifacts.mjs refuses to resolve a foreign provenance path implicitly and demands an explicit local cache root - correctly, because resolving someone else's absolute path against this filesystem is how a gate ends up verifying the wrong bytes. This file is where that root is named, so the gate carries no magic path and moving the cache is one reviewed line.
known: The current root sits under _to_delete/, which is a quarantine name and a poor home for the bytes a release deploys from. Moving it is a one-line change here plus a check-deploy-input allowlist entry; it has not been done because B3 refuses untracked files in the deployment surface and the move should land with that entry, not before it.
